h: Before you clip in: Reading know-how
p: Clip 'n Climb is one of those days out where a tiny bit of planning pays off big time. Here's what's worth knowing before you head over.

Paperwork first. Climbers need a participation form completing, and under-18s need a parent or guardian to sign, so get it sorted online at home if you can. It saves standing at the desk wrestling with a phone while the kids bounce off the walls in the other sense.

Next, ages. There's normally a minimum age for climbing and rules on supervising younger children, so read through them when you book. It's especially handy if you've got a big age spread in the family, as you'll know who can climb and who'll be cheering from the side.

Fuel matters more than you'd think. A light snack an hour or so before is perfect; a heavy pub lunch is not. Bring water, because twenty minutes of racing up walls is proper exercise even if it feels like messing about. Short nails and no rings help too.

How long to allow? Roughly a couple of hours from arriving to leaving, which leaves loads of the day for Reading. The Oracle shopping centre sits right on the River Kennet with places to eat along the water, Christchurch Meadows over in Caversham is great for a picnic and a play, and the National Trust's Basildon Park is a short drive out along the Thames valley for anyone wanting a grand house and gardens to finish.
